newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO, Israel say U.S. mission fails to end crisis.
newsitem.headline: PLO, Israel say U.S. mission fails to end crisis.

text.p: Israel said on Friday U.S.-brokered contacts with the PLO produced no progress towards reviving peace talks and accused Yasser Arafat of creating an "artificial crisis".

"The prime minister delivered a report to the ministers that there is no real progress in the contacts between us and the Palestinian Authority," the government said in a statement after the weekly cabinet meeting.
"There is an attempt, apparently, by the Palestinian Authority, by its leader, to create an artificial crisis," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh told Israel's army radio.
U.S. Middle East point man Dennis Ross was expected to leave for Washington later on Friday after coming up empty in his latest bid to breathe life into deadlocked Israeli-PLO peace moves.

Before leaving, Ross was to meet top Palestinian negotiators Saeb Erekat and Mahmoud Abbas, also known as Abu Mazen, Erekat told a news conference after he met European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos in the West Bank town of Jericho.
Ross met Moratinos and Israeli Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai separately in Jerusalem earlier on Friday.

All Ross had to show for his nine-day mission was a meeting last week between Israeli and PLO security chiefs that Israel denounced as insufficient and a second meeting between high-level political officials on Wednesday which Palestinians derided as a failure.
In a parting snub, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat declined to meet Ross on the eve of his return to Washington.
"Ross's mission has failed completely," Marwan Kanafani, a spokesman for Arafat, told Reuters.
A PLO official said Arafat had sent a letter to President Bill Clinton complaining indirectly at Ross's performance and asking Clinton to personally step in to salvage the peace.

Ross doggedly shuttled between the sides but failed to budge them from positions hardened during a two-month peace freeze sparked by Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement on an Arab East Jerusalem hilltop on March 18.

The PLO demands Israel order a halt to building Har Homa settlement on the windswept hill known to Palestinians as Jabal Abu Ghneim. It sees the settlement as an attempt to pre-empt final peace talks on the status of Jerusalem.

Netanyahu said this week he was proud of his approval of the settlement building. He conditioned resumption of negotiations on a PLO crackdown on "terror" after a Moslem militant killed himself and three Israelis in Tel Aviv on March 21.
Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy was due to meet U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright in Washington on Friday on the Middle East peace crisis.

Israeli President Ezer Weizman was quoted by an Israeli newspaper on Friday as saying he had cut contact with Netanyahu over his apparent lack of interest in Weizman's meeting with Arafat earlier this month.
Netanyahu's spokesman, Shai Bazak, said of the report: "As far as I know that isn't true." Weizman's spokesman was not available to comment.
"When I returned from the meeting with Arafat, I thought he would want to hear what happened there. Not at all," Yedioth quoted Weizman as saying.
